current_row.boundary_rationale: A restoration promise opens on a bare participial onset, not a dated formula in the bytes themselves — “In days to come, Jacob will take root. The argument continues through Isa.27.7's third-masculine-singular suffixes and Isa.27.8's third-feminine-singular suffixes, both read as referring back to Jacob and Israel of Isa.27.6 though carried by two different suffix classes rather than one repeated pronoun, through the atonement clause “the iniquity of Jacob will be forgiven” (web:Isa.27.9), matching יְכֻפַּ֣ר עֲוֺֽן יַעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.27.9, byte tier), and on to a contrastive judgment on an unnamed fortified city (web:Isa.27.10, web:Isa.27.11) offered as a foil to Jacob's own measured discipline. Isa.27.12 opens its own ba-yom-hahu formula, a fresh frame this row does not share.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A finer split at Isa.27.6 alone, corroborated by a single-witness setumah recorded there, was considered but rejected. Isa.27.7 opens not with a pronoun but with an interrogative-comparative construction, and its suffixes are third-masculine-singular, מַכֵּ֖הוּ הִכָּ֑הוּ (oshb:Isa.27.7, byte tier; the suffix class held as a byte-checkable claim, no morphology layer being staged); the referential link back to Jacob and Israel of Isa.27.6 is arguable from those 3ms forms, but Isa.27.8 shifts to third-feminine-singular suffixes instead, בְּשַׁלְחָ֣הּ תְּרִיבֶ֑נָּה (oshb:Isa.27.8, byte tier), a different suffix class rather than a continuation of the same one; the two verses are bound to Isa.27.6 by argument, not by one pronoun carried across all three.

A scroll-noun catchword crosses this row's front seam: הַסֵּ֣פֶר (oshb:Isa.29.11, byte tier) and סֵֽפֶר (oshb:Isa.29.12, byte tier) recur at consonantal-skeleton tier in דִּבְרֵי סֵ֑פֶר (oshb:Isa.29.18, byte tier), the noun's skeleton standing at exactly 4 verses in Isa.28-31 (oshb:Isa.29.11, oshb:Isa.29.12, oshb:Isa.29.18, oshb:Isa.30.8) and 20 book-wide. Isa.29.11's ketiv/qere variance sits later in that verse, outside the quoted word.

items.claim: The internal-cohesion bridge is quoted as two runs that do not match at the named skeleton tier, and carries no distribution digit.
items.proposed_change: Quote the shared verb alone on both sides at skeleton tier, keep the two context runs separately at byte tier, and add the 5-verse book-wide digit so the bridge's distinctiveness is on the record.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Confirmed. As quoted the bridge fails: הַיֹּצֵ֖ר יֵֽחָשֵׁ֑ב (oshb:Isa.29.16, byte tier) reaches tier none against the oshb:Isa.29.17 window, and וְהַכַּרְמֶ֖ל לַיַּ֥עַר יֵחָשֵֽׁב (oshb:Isa.29.17, byte tier) reaches tier none against oshb:Isa.29.16 - the claimed skeleton-tier sharing does not hold at the quoted extents. The shared verb alone holds, and only at skeleton tier: יֵֽחָשֵׁ֑ב (oshb:Isa.29.16, byte tier) collates at skeleton tier in oshb:Isa.29.17, and יֵחָשֵֽׁב (oshb:Isa.29.17, byte tier) at skeleton tier in oshb:Isa.29.16; both forms carry U+05BD at different positions and accent-stripping retains U+05BD, so skeleton is the lowest agreeing tier - the row's tier choice is right for the verb, wrong for its quoted runs. The bridge also ships without a distribution digit; re-swept, the verb's skeleton stands at 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses - oshb:Isa.10.7, oshb:Isa.13.17, oshb:Isa.29.16, oshb:Isa.29.17, oshb:Isa.32.15). The row's stated internal-cohesion evidence is byte-true in substance yet defectively quoted and un-digited: medium as filed, not high.

items.claim: The '20 book-wide' scroll-noun digit is a bare substring count blending a place name, a different noun, and a verb family.
items.proposed_change: Either restrict the book-wide digit to the scroll noun by sweeping its attested spellings and naming them, or drop the book-wide figure and keep the in-window 4-verse digit, which is sound.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Confirmed. Re-swept, the contiguous skeleton substring ספר stands at exactly 20 verses book-wide (sweep: 20 verses) and exactly 4 in Isa.28-31 (sweep: 4 verses - oshb:Isa.29.11, oshb:Isa.29.12, oshb:Isa.29.18, oshb:Isa.30.8), every in-window matching token the scroll noun, so the in-window digit is sound. The 20 blends count objects: it includes the number noun מִסְפָּ֣ר (oshb:Isa.10.19, byte tier; also oshb:Isa.21.17, oshb:Isa.40.26), the scribe noun סֹפֵר֙ (oshb:Isa.33.18, byte tier; also oshb:Isa.36.3), the recount-verb family סְפַרְתֶּ֑ם (oshb:Isa.22.10, byte tier; also oshb:Isa.43.21, oshb:Isa.43.26, oshb:Isa.52.15 - two sites beyond the finding's floor, its 'at minimum' hedge holding), and the place name סְפַרְוָ֑יִם (oshb:Isa.36.19, byte tier; also oshb:Isa.37.13): 11 of the 20 verses carry no scroll-noun token. The finding's K/Q check also re-derives: 1 K/Q note at oshb:Isa.29.11 (single-witness), and the quoted הַסֵּ֣פֶר (oshb:Isa.29.11, byte tier) stands before the staged doubled pair הספר סֵ֛פֶר (oshb:Isa.29.11, byte tier, first token the unpointed ketiv) later in the verse. A digit attributed to the named noun while counting a blended substring family is a defective count claim on a disclosure device, not a boundary carrier: medium as filed.

items.claim: The rear-edge warrant asserts a koh-amar frame at Isa.29.22 with no pointed splice, no oshb ref, and no frame owner named.
items.proposed_change: Splice לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.29.22, byte tier) into the closing sentence, name it a divine frame, and add oshb:Isa.29.22 to boundary_evidence_refs.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Confirmed. The shipped rear edge argues the koh-amar address from the rendering over web:Isa.29.22 - no oshb:Isa.29.22 in boundary_evidence_refs, and the closing sentence names no frame owner (re-checked). The claim is byte-true and verse-initial: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.29.22, byte tier), the tetragrammaton standing as speaker - a divine frame, and oshb:Isa.29.22 is not among the four royal-messenger koh-amar sites (oshb:Isa.36.4, oshb:Isa.36.14, oshb:Isa.36.16, oshb:Isa.37.3), the ruled role split that requires every koh-amar claim to name whose frame it engages. Rendering-only support plus the unnamed frame owner make a defective rear-edge warrant under the mandatory pointed-splice discipline; the edge itself is correct and co-warranted by the quoted close at web:Isa.29.21 with its disclosed single-witness setumah: medium as filed.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A consequence connector opens this row, וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽחֲנַנְכֶ֔ם (oshb:Isa.30.18, byte tier), the same particle recurring a second time later in the same verse; the bare particle stands at exactly 25 verses book-wide at consonantal-skeleton tier and is the same connector, לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Isa.30.12, byte tier), that opens the indictment frame earlier in this chapter, so the turn is argued as a consequence rather than a fresh temporal onset. “Therefore Yahweh will wait, that he may be gracious to you” (web:Isa.30.18) turns away from the flight-and-siege verdict closing at web:Isa.30.17. The speaker changes there -- divine first-person address under the frame at oshb:Isa.30.15 (גְּבֽוּרַתְכֶ֑ם, אֲבִיתֶֽם) and at oshb:Isa.30.17 (תָּנֻ֑סוּ, נוֹתַרְתֶּ֗ם) gives way to third-person report at Isa.30.18 -- but the second-person plural ADDRESSEE carries across the seam: Isa.30.18's object suffixes answer the same second-person plural running through Isa.30.15 and Isa.30.17. That addressee continuity, not a continuing speaking voice, is the seam's real warrant. The promise runs through restored teachers, rejected idols, and agricultural blessing without a further frame break, closing on “heals the wound they were struck with.” (web:Isa.30.26), the verse just before the theophany onset at web:Isa.30.27.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival cut would separate the graciousness promise (Isa.30.18-Isa.30.19) from the agricultural blessing (Isa.30.23-Isa.30.26) as two distinct oracles.
current_row.literature_type_guess: Zion promise oracle of grace, restored teachers, and agricultural abundance

items.claim: The row names a byte-true cross-seam continuity fact as 'the seam's real warrant' for its own front cut, and no tier-1 onset class stands in its opening verse's bytes.
items.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): restate the addressee continuity as the disclosed cross-seam cohesion it is, name the ground the onset verse's own bytes carry, and register the frame-onset deviation or lower the band. Disagreement with the row's stated grounds — routed onward, not adjudicated here.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived both ways. The finding quotes the row's warrant sentence accurately, and the continuity facts are byte-true: גְּבֽוּרַתְכֶ֑ם (oshb:Isa.30.15, byte tier) and אֲבִיתֶֽם (oshb:Isa.30.15, byte tier), with תָּנֻ֑סוּ (oshb:Isa.30.17, byte tier) and נוֹתַרְתֶּ֗ם (oshb:Isa.30.17, byte tier), carry the second-person plural that the suffix inside the row's own opener וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽחֲנַנְכֶ֔ם (oshb:Isa.30.18, byte tier) answers. That is cross-seam cohesion straddling the row's own front seam: under the cross-seam law it argues continuity against the cut, so disclosing it is right and naming it 'the seam's real warrant' is a defective warrant. The opening verse's bytes carry a backward-linking consequence connector as first token -- no hoy, no massa, no koh-amar frame, no imperative or vocative onset (first-token and bigram checks, skeleton tier) -- and the row itself states the addressee does not shift. The tier-3 layer re-derives exactly as the finding states: chapter-30 segs are SAMEKH at MT 30:5, 30:11, 30:18, 30:26, 30:33 with PE at MT 30:14, none at MT 30:17, so the nearest marked division falls after the row's opening verse, interior to the span. With only the consequence-connector signal registered, no frame-onset deviation, and frontier_flag_considered false, the warrant defect is real but not alone load-bearing -- the verdict-to-promise turn and the rear seam stand: medium as filed.

items.claim: The 25-verse digit belongs to the substring class that blends bare and waw-prefixed forms, not to 'the bare particle' the prose names; the bare particle stands at 23 verses, and the row's own onset is the waw-prefixed form.
items.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): either cite 23 verses for the bare particle and disclose that this row's own onset is the waw-prefixed form, or keep 25 and name the swept object as the skeleton class including waw-prefixed forms.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-swept from bytes. The contiguous consonantal-skeleton substring returns exactly 25 MT verses (staged sweep, verse unit); the word-bound token split of that same hit set is clean: the bare token לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Isa.30.12, byte tier) stands in 23 verses, the waw-prefixed form in exactly 2 -- MT 8:7 and MT 30:18 -- no verse carries both forms, and no third token shape exists in the hit set. The row's 25 digit therefore belongs to the blended substring class while its prose names 'the bare particle', which stands at 23; and the row's own onset is waw-prefixed -- both connector tokens of MT 30:18 are: וְלָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Isa.30.18, byte tier) and וְלָכֵ֥ן (oshb:Isa.30.18, byte tier) -- while the comparator at MT 30:12 the prose calls 'the same connector' is bare, a form difference never disclosed. A digit attached to the wrong named object beside a warrant, not alone load-bearing: medium as filed.

current_row.boundary_rationale: This unit opens at הֵ֥ן לְצֶ֖דֶק יִמְלָךְ מֶ֑לֶךְ וּלְשָׂרִ֖ים לְמִשְׁפָּ֥ט יָשֹֽׂרוּ (oshb:Isa.32.1, byte tier), “Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in justice.” (web:Isa.32.1), a fresh topic onset describing a future righteous ruler; the closing signature at oshb:Isa.31.9 does not carry its own addressee forward into this new topic. The presentative הֵ֥ן opening this verse stands verse-initial at exactly 18 verses book-wide, only two of them in chapters 28-35 -- this site and oshb:Isa.33.7 -- so the particle alone does not discriminate the two; what distinguishes this site is the topic itself, a coming king unconnected to anything preceding it, where the parallel site continues describing an already-open scene rather than opening one. The span continues describing the ruler's effect and the noble-versus-scoundrel contrast through oshb:Isa.32.8 and closes there, immediately before the vocative onset that opens the following unit at oshb:Isa.32.9, “Rise up, you women who are at ease! Hear my voice!” oshb:Isa.31.9, the verse immediately ahead of this unit's own onset, is closed by a parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness); at the unit's own close, oshb:Isa.32.8 carries a parashah PE mark (single-witness) corroborating the break.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A split at web:Isa.32.5, where the description sharpens from noble rule in general to the fool-and-scoundrel contrast in particular, found no support: no addressee or frame shift accompanies that sharpening, and the passage continues describing the same righteous order through web:Isa.32.8.
current_row.literature_type_guess: oracle of a future righteous king and his officials

items.claim: The 18-verse digit for the verse-initial presentative names no tier, holds only at skeleton tier, and its eighteenth member there is a ketiv token rather than the pointed presentative the row names; the pointed form stands verse-initial at 17.
items.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): cite 17 verses at accent-stripped tier for the pointed presentative, or keep 18 while naming the skeleton tier and disclosing the MT 54:16 ketiv member.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-swept on first-token identity. Verse-initial matching gives 18 MT verses at consonantal-skeleton tier and 17 at accent-stripped tier; the sole delta member is MT 54:16, a K/Q verse (single-witness inventory, 1 note) whose verse-initial token is the unpointed ketiv הן (oshb:Isa.54.16, byte tier) standing before the pointed qere הִנֵּ֤ה (oshb:Isa.54.16, byte tier) -- at the pointed layer that verse opens with the hinneh presentative, not the hen form at all. The row's own splice הֵ֥ן (oshb:Isa.32.1, byte tier) is the pointed presentative and its digit names no tier, so 18 is mis-owned exactly as claimed: it holds only at skeleton tier and only by counting a ketiv skeleton, the class the K/Q-before-counting rule guards; the pointed form stands verse-initial at 17. The dependent sub-claim survives at both tiers -- the only chapters-28-35 members are MT 32:1 and MT 33:7. An untiered, K/Q-contaminated digit, not alone load-bearing (the row rests the site's discrimination on topic, not on the count): medium as filed.

items.claim: device_notes lists a parashah mark as one of the three grounds the boundary rests on; in the Prophets the layer is tier-3 weak corroboration and never a boundary driver.
items.proposed_change: Field repair (proposal only): restate the PE as tier-3 corroboration of the rear seam and remove it from the list of grounds the boundary rests on.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Mark facts re-derived from the inventory: PE at MT 32:8 -- correctly typed, correctly not conflated with the SAMEKH segs at MT 31:9 and MT 32:20 -- and disclosed single-witness by the row. The defect is weight: device_notes reads 'resting the boundary on the fresh subject (the coming king), the verse-initial presentative, and the parashah PE mark at oshb:Isa.32.8', listing a Prophets parashah mark among the grounds the boundary rests on; under the owner addendum that layer is tier-3 weak corroboration, never a boundary driver, and the row's own boundary_rationale holds the same mark to 'corroborating the break'. The two fields assign the same mark different weights and the device_notes phrasing is the defective one. Not alone load-bearing -- the topic onset and the presentative carry the seam: medium as filed.
